## Critique
- claim-1: The partition enumeration and unitriangular minors are mathematically correct once the relevant presentation is assumed. However, the argument silently identifies “degree-\(d+k\) columns” with Schur classes \(s_\mu\) satisfying \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\). An integral box Schur basis alone does not supply this column-indexing statement or establish that all \(h_1\)-rows arise by multiplying every degree-\(d+k-1\) column. These presentation facts must be explicitly assumed, derived, or grounded. The Pieri argument should also explicitly exclude every other addable box. Thus the strategy proves the requested combinatorial result conditionally, but the requested target is not established unconditionally or from the stated hypotheses alone.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Prove or explicitly invoke the presentation statement
  \[
  M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+k}}\mathbb Zs_\mu
  \]
  and that its complete \(h_1\)-row set is \(\{h_1s_\lambda:|\lambda|=d+k-1\}\). Then show that the only in-box additions to \(P_{x,k-1-x}\) are \(P_{x+1,k-1-x}\) and \(P_{x,k-x}\).
- [computation] Supply an executable partition-enumeration checker which, for specified \(i,j\), tests every \(0\le k\le\min(i,j)\), verifies the complete column and one-box-extension lists, and computes both complementary determinants as \(1\). This is finite corroboration only.
- [source-refresh] Supply a stable source excerpt grounding the exact presentation facts that columns are indexed by the interval \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\) and that the complete \(h_1\)-rows are the corresponding Pieri multiplication rows.

## Required revisions
- State the column-indexing and row-completeness hypotheses explicitly.
- Add the exclusion argument for all other Pieri additions.
- State the row lattice and both endpoint minors explicitly in the formal claim, not only in the strategy.
- Report the conclusion as conditional unless the missing presentation facts are proved or grounded.
